dice.title: Dice
dice.expressionHint: Dice, numbers, kh or kl to keep the highest or lowest, and damage tags in brackets.
dice.emptyHint: Enter an expression and roll; results show here.
dice.dcHint: The kept roll is compared with this DC for a degree of success.
dice.targetHint: The kept roll is dealt to this target as damage. Untagged dice and numbers are untyped.
dice.persistentTaken: Persistent damage: {taken} at the end of each turn

rules.title: Rules
rules.description: Check rules data against Pioneer’s schemas: predicates, selectors, domains, roll options, sources, origins, rule elements and content entries, try a formula with your own reference values, see whether a predicate holds, or derive statistics from their definitions.
rules.schemaHint: Changing the schema loads a valid example for it.
rules.jsonHint: Strings need double quotes, as in any JSON.
rules.formulaHint: Numbers, + - * /, brackets, @ references like @level or @attr.str, and functions like max and floor.
rules.formulaValid: The formula as Pioneer prints it:
rules.referencesHint: A value for each @ reference in the formula. Clear a box to leave its reference without a value.
rules.referenceInvalid: Enter a whole number from {minimum} to {maximum}. Until then, this reference has no value.
rules.referenceUnknown: Pioneer has no such reference, so stored formulas cannot use it.
rules.referenceFoundry: This is Foundry’s spelling. Stored formulas write {suggestion}.
rules.formulaTree: Parsed tree, with each part’s position:
rules.factsHint: One per line, like self:level:5 or terrain:forest. A missing self, feat or class option counts as false; a missing terrain, target or action option is unknown.
rules.badFacts: {count, plural, one {Line {lines} is not a roll option.} other {Lines {lines} are not roll options.}}
rules.factsNotChecked: Fix the roll options to see the verdict.
rules.statisticsHint: A JSON array of statistic definitions. A statistic reads another one’s base with @stat, like @stat.spell-attack.arcane.
rules.inputsHint: Level, the six attribute modifiers, a proficiency rank per selector (a selector left out is untrained) and an optional Dexterity cap.
rules.grantEntriesHint: A JSON array of entries, each with a slug, a name and rule elements. A GrantItem may name its entry by slug here. An entry is a class feature unless it gives a kind, and is on the character as the roll option its kind sets, like feature:bravery, or feat:sudden-charge for an entry of kind feat. A ChoiceSet query reads an entry’s rollOptions, like trait:fighter, as item:trait:fighter.
rules.grantRootsHint: The slugs of the entries the character has directly, one per line, like fighter or woodland-elf. A condition may take its value after the slug, a whole number from 1, like frightened 2.
rules.badRoots: {count, plural, one {Line {lines} is not a slug, or a condition’s slug and a whole number from 1.} other {Lines {lines} are not slugs, or conditions’ slugs and whole numbers from 1.}}
rules.grantPicksHint: One choice per line: the entry’s slug and the ChoiceSet’s rule index, then the picked value, like fighter:4 = sudden-charge. A value that is an entry’s slug picks that entry.
rules.badPicks: {count, plural, one {Line {lines} is not a pick.} other {Lines {lines} are not picks.}}
rules.grantLevelHint: The character’s level, read as self:level. Class features gated on it arrive and leave as it changes.
rules.badLevel: A level is a whole number from {min} to {max}.
rules.grantTogglesHint: One toggleable RollOption per line: the entry’s slug and its rule index, then on, off or a suboption to turn it on with, like fighter:7 = on. A toggle left out starts at its value.
rules.badToggles: {count, plural, one {Line {lines} is not a toggle.} other {Lines {lines} are not toggles.}}
rules.grantFactsHint: Situational roll options, one per line, like terrain:forest. The character’s own facts come from the level field and the entries on it, so self, feat, feature and other known options typed here are left out.
rules.noGrants: Nothing is on the character yet.
rules.filterQueryHint: URL query params, one per facet: f.traits=fire,!evil picks entries with the fire trait and none with evil; f.level=1..5 bounds a range, and either end may be left out. Values in one facet combine with OR, facets with AND.
rules.filterEntriesHint: A JSON array of content entries, any kinds. The facets offered are those of the kinds in the list.
rules.filterKept: {kept, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} of {total} kept.
rules.filterNoQuery: No filters: every entry is kept.
rules.noOptions: Nothing can be picked for this choice yet.

verdict.unknown: The predicate depends on the situation: some roll options it needs were not given.

rules.valid: Valid. This is the value as Pioneer reads it:
rules.notJson: This is not valid JSON yet. Check quotes, commas and brackets.
rules.entryKindHint: Picking another kind loads a valid entry of it. The kind field decides which schema checks data.
rules.statisticSourceHint: Picking a source replaces the definitions with its statistics.
rules.statisticSourceFailed: The pack did not load. Pick it again to retry.
rules.invalidSummary: {count, plural, one {# problem, listed under Result.} other {# problems, listed under Result.}}
rules.nothingToShow: Nothing to check until the JSON parses.
rules.ruleElementsHint: A JSON array of rule elements, numbered from 1 in the order written. FlatModifier adds a bonus or penalty; AdjustModifier changes or suppresses one by its slug.
rules.overridesHint: Rule elements set by hand, numbered from 1. A FlatModifier is an adjust override and stacks as usual; a Change with mode override is a set override and pins the total.
rules.overrideEffect: {mode, select, add {add} multiply {multiply} upgrade {at least} downgrade {at most} other {set}}: {replaced} to {result}
